objects.boundary: BrowserContext does not define native profile persistence, locking, policy, or budgets
CDP session is a client attachment, not the native engine authority
observed by the synthetic G2 court; HTML engines and external clients remain unqualified

one-to-one with a native frame while both live, adapter-scoped and not stable across adapters; qualified through Page.getFrameTree on the synthetic host (main frame plus one bounded child) and on the native route (one main frame) where puppeteer-core 24.15.0 observes it over a loopback edge and keeps the same id across a same-frame navigation; Page.frameNavigated and child-frame nesting are not projected; document generation has no CDP equivalent

realm identity and retirement are native; no Runtime.enable, executionContextCreated or executionContextDestroyed is projected in this increment, so a CDP client cannot observe realm replacement except through stale DOM handles after navigation
target activation is not presentation attachment
maintained by the native target and adapter
CDP IDs never bypass target revision validation

losses.loss: no CDP concept; Page.loaderId is the closest and is not mapped
no target.navigate exists in 0.0.1; the synthetic host navigates through a link click and projects no navigation events

both hosts project child frames flat and offer no nesting: the synthetic host has exactly one bounded child frame, which proves the tree shape and the identity mapping only, and its adapter substitutes the target or court address for that child because it has no document of its own to name; the native host builds bounded, same-origin, depth-one children and is the route qualified to project each frame's own final url
only the main world exists on the synthetic host; isolated worlds are unprojected

setTimeout and clearTimeout exist natively in the main frame and are not projected: Runtime.evaluate and Emulation.setVirtualTimePolicy are absent methods and answer -32601, while Runtime.callFunctionOn exists and is qualified for exactly one declaration, so a timer declaration answers -32602 as an unaccepted parameter rather than a missing method; setInterval, animation frames, idle callbacks and workers do not exist natively either
